Based on the search results, here's information about Entire.io CLI installation and the "entire enable" command for Windows session capture with Git:

## Installation

For Windows, you can install stable via Scoop or via the install.sh script using `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash`. On Windows with Scoop, run `scoop bucket add entire https://github.com/entireio/scoop-bucket.git` followed by `scoop install entire/entire`.

## Enabling Entire in Your Repository

On a repo that has not been enabled yet, `entire enable` runs the initial enable flow: it creates Entire settings, installs git hooks, and prompts you to choose which agent hooks to install.

## Session Capture and Git Integration

Entire CLI hooks into your Git workflow to capture AI agent sessions as you work. The hooks capture session data as you work, and checkpoints are created when you or the agent make a git commit.

Your code commits stay clean, Entire never creates commits on your active branch. Instead, all session metadata is stored on a separate entire/checkpoints/v1 branch.

## Available Options

You can specify an agent with `entire enable --agent <name>` to work with your AI agent (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, or Copilot CLI).

# Installing and Enabling Entire CLI

## Installation

The CLI supports multiple platforms with these installation methods:

**macOS/Linux with Homebrew:**
```
brew install --cask entireio/tap/entire
```

**macOS/Linux without Homebrew:**
```
curl -fsSL https://entire.com/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows (PowerShell 5.1+):**
```
irm https://entire.com/install.ps1 | iex
```

For prerelease builds, add `@nightly` to the Homebrew command or `--channel nightly` to the shell scripts.

The system requires Git to be installed on your machine. Additional installation methods (Scoop, `go install`) are documented at docs.entire.com/installation.

## Enabling in a Repository

Once installed, initialize capture in your project directory:

```
cd your-project
entire enable                    # select your agents; installs hooks
entire status                    # view current sessions and checkpoint upload locations
```

**What gets installed:** The `entire enable` command sets up Git hooks for capturing agent work without disrupting any existing hooks you've configured. It installs Entire's hooks alongside your current setup.

**Key behavior:** The system creates checkpoints—capturing prompts, transcripts, and modified files—linked to commits via git trailers. These are stored as Git refs (`refs/entire/checkpoints/…`) rather than added as commits to your branch.

content.text:
Entire CLI 0.12.2 is installed and enabled for Claude Code in this repo. `entire status` shows it as enabled on `master`. I haven't committed anything, and I haven't checked that it captures a session yet.

- **Install:** I used `go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@latest`. The binary is at `C:\Users\Lenovo\go\bin\entire.exe`, which is already on your PATH.
- **What the enable step added:** `entire enable --agent claude-code` created `.entire/settings.json`, `.entire/.gitignore` and `.claude/settings.json`. It also installed 10 Claude Code hooks, plus git hooks that sit alongside any existing ones. These files are untracked, and Entire asks you to commit them so it works across clones and worktrees.
- **Where sessions go:** Checkpoints link to your commits through git trailers. Entire stores them under `refs/entire/checkpoints/…`, not as commits on `master`.

**Before you push:** Checkpoints upload to `origin` when you push, and they contain your full agent transcripts. If the repo is public, anyone can read them, and Entire's secret redaction is best effort.
- Run `entire checkpoint explain` to review a checkpoint before you push.
- To keep them out of `origin`, run `entire configure --local --checkpoint-remote github:<owner>/<repo>` to use a separate private repo.
- To stop uploads, run `entire configure --local --skip-push-sessions`.

Entire also found earlier Claude Code history for this project. `entire import claude-code` would pull it in, but I didn't run it. Your M0 and M1 commits predate Entire, so that import is how they'd get transcripts. I assumed the agent name is `claude-code`; check `entire import --help` if it errors.
